UB01.why: Solve V = (1/3)πr²h for h: isolates a plain factor. UB01 must undo a square root (divide by 2π, square the whole side, multiply by g). Different key step. Cited.
Area in terms of circumference: substitute r = C/(2π). Different mechanism. Cited.

UB02.why: Border on all four sides of a square photo, (s + 4)² − s². UB02 trims two sides of a non-square rectangle and rejects the root 44. Cited.
Rectangle-to-square and open-box domain. Different ask. Cited.

UB03.why: (x + 3)² from x² + 6x = 7: one-variable square completion. Cited.
x² + y² = 29 and xy = 10, find (x + y)²: two-variable square identity, different given and ask. Not cited.
Combine two linear equations into a target linear expression. Cited.

UB04.why: f(1/x) = −f(x) for a rational f: substitution, not self-composition. Cited.
Simplify a written-out compound fraction. UB04 must build it by composing. Cited.
f(f(x)) with polynomials or numbers (count roots, evaluate, solve). None composes a rational function symbolically.

UB05.why: (x − 3)(x + 5) = (x − 3)(2x − 1), sum of solutions; dividing loses x = 3. UB05 turns the lost root into the condition for a parameter. Cited.

x² + (k − 2)x + k − 3 = 0 has exactly one solution; discriminant is a perfect square in k. UB05's discriminant is also a perfect square, (k − 5)², but it asks for k, not the solution, and the factored form is visible. Not cited.
c(x − 4) + 12 = 3x with exactly one solution (linear, asks the solution). Different degree and ask.

UB06.why: Generator flag adjudicated: ACT-618 evaluates n(n − 1)/2 forward for n = 8 (answer 28). UB06 gives the count and solves the quadratic for n, rejecting −12. Different asked quantity and key step. Allowed; keep in a different batch from any handshake/diagonal count.
Diagonals of a 10-gon, n(n − 3)/2 forward. Different ask.

UB07.why: Vertex of y = x² − 8x + c on y = x; find c. UB07 finds b from a slope in which c cancels. Cited.
Vertex-position conditions with a known b; different ask. 000615 cited.

UB08.why: Interval where a given quadratic is positive. UB08 recovers a from the y-intercept and uses the threshold −5 (mirror point). Cited.
Quadratic profit at least 600, count whole-dollar prices: quadratic inequality against a nonzero threshold, but the quadratic is given and the ask is a count.

UB09.why: Square inscribed in a 6-8 right triangle in the same position; single shape, no optimization. The square is UB09's trap. Cited.
Greatest perimeter of a rectangle under a parabola. Cited.
Square on one side of a triangle with height 10; similar triangles, no optimization.

UB10.why: Find c from shifted or given roots. Cited.
Sum and product of roots used forward. UB10 makes the coefficients the roots, a system in b and c.

UB11.why: Integer k for which x² + kx + 9 = 0 has no real solutions; discriminant k² − 36. Cited.
Two real solutions, condition linear in k. Cited.
k in both the linear and the constant term (000794), and an interval MC for a discriminant condition (PB09, 0 < c < 9). UB11 combines the two; different ask from each.

UB12.why: Not cited. ACT-101: if 2^a = 3 and 3^b = 16, what is ab? (4). UB12: if 2^a = 5 and 5^b = 8, what is ab? (3). Same chained-base mechanism (2^(ab) = (2^a)^b), same asked quantity (ab), same distractor types (6.34 = calculator decimal, 48 = product of outputs). Cross-exam re-skin with only numbers changed. Drop.

UB13.why: Not cited. ACT-049: if x + 1/x = 5, what is x² + 1/x²? (23). UB13: f(x) = 3^x + 3^(−x), f(a) = 5, find f(2a) (23). With u = 3^a, this is exactly u + 1/u = 5, find u² + 1/u², with the same given 5, the same answer 23 and the same traps (25, 27). The exponential wrapper adds only the rewrite 9^a = (3^a)². Drop.

UB13.other_id: CLD-SAT-M-000836 (= ideas-gen-23 RB05, batch-076) / CLD-SAT-M-000466 / CLD-SAT-M-000287
UB13.why: Reciprocal-pair identities (difference of squares; (√x + 1/√x)²; x + 1/x from a quadratic). Different asks. 836 cited.

UB14.why: Pull a constant out of a shifted exponent (2^(x+1) = 2 · 2^x). UB14 also merges 2^x · 3^x into 6^x. Different ask.

UB15.why: Not cited (generator cited ACT-467 instead). ACT-290: a rectangle has a perimeter of 34 centimeters and an area of 60 square centimeters; what is the length of its longer side? (12). UB15: perimeter 34 cm, area 70 cm², longer side (10). Same mechanism (sum and product give a quadratic whose roots are the sides), same ask, even the same perimeter and units. Only the area changes. Drop.
Perimeter and diagonal give the area; no quadratic solved. Cited.

UB16.why: a/b from a linear relation. Cited.

UB17.why: Half-life given, compute forward. UB17 recovers the half-life. Cited.
Doubling/halving period given; different ask (percent per sub-period; time to equal).

UD01.why: One external tangency: center distance = sum of radii. Cited.
Common external tangent of two circles. Different ask. TD08 cited.

UD02.why: Longest rod in a 3-by-4-by-12 box: edges given. UD02 must recover a² + b² + c² from face diagonals. Cited.
Face areas to volume; vertex to face center. Cited.

UD03.why: 3:4:5 shape given and scaled. UD03 derives the shape from the arithmetic-sequence condition. Cited.

UD04.why: Single semicircle attached to a polygon. Cited.
Square in a semicircle; running-track area. Different setup.

UD05.why: Hemisphere poured into a cylinder; find a depth. Cited.
Volume scaling of a cylinder; sphere displacement. Different ask.

UD06.why: Generator flag adjudicated: ACT-617 gives the interior angle (150°) and asks n. UD06 asks the same final quantity (n from a regular polygon's interior angle), but the angle (156°) must first be built from the 360° around the point and the decagon's interior angle (144°), which is two added steps. Close, not template. Allowed; keep apart from ACT-617, ACT-186 and ACT-657.
Square and regular pentagon share a side; find an angle. Cited.

UD07.why: Cos of an angle in one right triangle; similar-triangle side ratio. Cited.

UD08.why: Diameter AB, inscribed angle at C; find angles/arcs. UD08 works backward from an area to r. Cited.
Area of triangle AOB as k√3 from an arc; 30-60-90 split. Different setup.

UD09.why: Cylinder inscribed in a sphere. Cited.
Cone radius at a known water level by similar triangles. Cited.

UD10.why: Corner triangles cut from a rectangle; point inside a square. Different ask.

UD11.why: Right angle at the origin inscribed in a known circle. UD11 uses the right angle to locate the diameter of an unknown circle. Cited.
Circle through two points tangent to a line; radius is also 13/2 = 6.5. Different mechanism but the same answer: keep apart. Cited.
Circle of radius 13 through two points; center by perpendicular bisector. Different ask.

UD12.why: Not cited. Two poles 6 and 9 m tall, crossed wires, crossing height 3.6 = ab/(a + b). Each half of UD12's segment is the same ab/(a + b) quantity (6 = 15·10/25) from the same crossed-segments similar-triangle mechanism; UD12 asks for a length in a trapezoid and doubles it. Different asked quantity and setting, so close, but a strong mechanism match: never batch together.
Diagonal split ratio used for areas (752), a diagonal piece (193), the midsegment (333). Cited.

UD13.why: 25-foot ladder, base moved from 7 to 15 ft; how far the top slides (4). UD13: same 25-foot ladder and 7-24-25 triple, same kind of ask (change in the top's height, 17). The added step is decoding a sine and a cosine (cofunction), so close rather than template, but the surface is nearly identical. Revise numbers (different ladder and triple). Cited.

UD13.other_id: CLD-SAT-M-000858 (= ideas-gen-23 RD09, batch-077) / CLD-SAT-M-000801 / CLD-SAT-M-000802 (batch-073) / CLD-ACT-M-000401
UD13.why: Cofunction family: kite height from cos(90 − x)° = 0.6; sin A = cos B triangle area; sin(90 − x) + cos(90 − x); cos(90° − θ). Four live cofunction items already; UD13 is the fifth. Allowed, but keep apart from all of these. 858 cited.

within_list_cues.UB03: Plug-in cue (generator flag adjudicated): the expression is constant on the line, so x = 3, y = 0 gives 9 − 6 = 3 instantly and eliminates all three distractors without any factoring. This is a non-identity item, so the point check is a full bypass, not a check. Not a drop (the recognition skill is real and the SAT has similar items), but rate it easy-medium, not medium, and do not count it as a factoring item. An SPR version does not fix it.
within_list_cues.UB16: Plug-in concern (generator flag adjudicated): testing choices in x² − 5xy + 6y² = 0 with y = 1 rejects A (1/3) and D (6) and leaves 2 and 3; the stated condition x ≠ 2y then picks 3. Back-solving a choice is ordinary MC strategy and still uses the condition, so this is acceptable. Unlike UB03, the plug-in does not bypass the item. Keep at medium-hard. Minor: B is ruled out by the stem's own condition, so it is a weak distractor for careful readers; D (6) is weak too. Consider replacing D with 3/2 (solves for y/x after factoring as (x − 2y)(x − 3y) and inverting the excluded root) or −3 (sign slip in the factors).
within_list_cues.UB06: Easy SPR: 13 can be found by trying n with a calculator (13·12/2 = 78). Acceptable at easy. Trap 12 rationale fine.
within_list_cues.UB12: Calculator shortcut: log₂5 × log₅8 = 3.000 on any calculator. Moot (drop).
within_list_cues.UB14: Calculator/Desmos shortcut: graph y = 2^(x + 1)·3^(x − 1) and y = 16, read x ≈ 1.6826, then 6^x = 24.000. The exact integer key makes the purely numeric route fully reliable, so the exponent-rule skill can be skipped. Not fatal (the SAT allows Desmos), but this is a cue. Consider asking for an expression rather than a number, or keep it at medium.
within_list_cues.UB15: Moot (drop). The key 10 and the trap 7 are the two roots, so a student can guess 10 by finding two numbers with sum 17 and product 70 by inspection.
within_list_cues.UB05: Mild: 3 is visible in the factor (x − 3) and is listed as a trap; the key 5 is not visible. Fine.
within_list_cues.UB11: Mild: test values k = 0, 4 and 6 (substitute and check for real roots) eliminate B, C and D, but each test needs the discriminant or a factoring check, so it is not a bypass. Fine.
within_list_cues.UD07: Irrelevant given: ST = 50 is never used. This is the intended bait for A (7/50), and the item is easy, so it is acceptable, but the item reviewer should know. Choices are short and not distinguishable by length.
within_list_cues.UD10: Mild: C (10√2 ≈ 14.14) is within 0.15 of the key 14, but it is distinct in exact form, so this is fine. The 6-8-10 triple is guessable from AE = 6 and side 10, so the item stays at medium.
within_list_cues.UD11: Same answer as banked CLD-SAT-M-000673 (6.5). Not a cue in itself, but keep the two in different batches.
within_list_cues.UD06: Scope note: interior angles of regular polygons ((n − 2)·180/n) are not an explicit digital-SAT topic. They are rarely tested on the SAT and common on the ACT. Acceptable as a hard geometry item, but do not add more of these.
within_list_cues.UD02: Scope note: the space diagonal √(a² + b² + c²) of a box is rare on the digital SAT (it appears only as a Pythagorean extension). Acceptable at hard. The item can be solved by recovering the edges 2, 3, 6, which is pure Pythagorean work.
within_list_cues.UD13: Mild: the trap 0 ('the same angle') is common-sense-eliminable, because the base moved, so the height changed. The 25-7-24 numbers repeat CLD-ACT-M-000241 exactly.
within_list_cues.UD01: Good: r > 2 removes the other configuration, (√17 − 3)/2 ≈ 0.56. The trap √5 ≈ 2.236 satisfies r > 2, so it stays plausible.
within_list_cues.within-list overlaps (generator-noted): UD08/UD11: both rely on 'an inscribed right angle subtends a diameter'. Allowed as different items (one area-to-radius with a 30-60-90 triangle, one coordinate radius), but put them in different batches. UB03/UB16: both two-variable quadratic forms in x and y that factor; different asks; separate batches. UB12–UB14: UB12 and UB13 are dropped, so UB14 is the only live exponent item from the trio. UB02/UB06/UB15: UB15 is dropped; UB02 and UB06 both 'set up a quadratic from context and reject a root', so keep them apart. UD07/UD09/UD12: UD09 and UD12 both use similar triangles to get a linear length relation, so separate them; UD07 overlaps only loosely.

math_errors.none (keys): All 30 keys and every listed distractor or trap were recomputed with sympy (scratchpad v74.py). UB01 L = gT²/(4π²) (check 1.000); UB02 roots 6, 44, trap 5.28; UB03 3 (6, 9, 15 check); UB04 (x − 1)/x, at x = 2: A 1, B 2, C −0.5, D 0.5; UB05 (x − 3)(x + 2 − k), discriminant (k − 5)², k = 5; UB06 13 (−12; 12 from n(n + 1)/2; 9.35); UB07 slope = b/2 for all c, b = −6; UB08 a = 1, 0 < x < 4, q = 4; UB09 max 20 at x = 5, square trap 1600/81 = 19.75, inverted-slope trap 12.8; UB10 (b, c) = (1, −2), spurious (−1/2, −1/2) and (0, 0) excluded, x² − x/2 − 1/2 has roots 1 and −1/2; UB11 −2 < k < 6; UB12 ab = 3 (a ≈ 2.3219, b ≈ 1.2920); UB13 23 (both roots of u + 1/u = 5); UB14 6^x = 24, A 32/3, D 96; UB15 7, 10; UB16 2, 3; UB17 h = 2; UD01 r = 3, (√17 − 3)/2 ≈ 0.56, √5 ≈ 2.236; UD02 a², b², c² = 4, 9, 36 → 7, √98 ≈ 9.90, √85 ≈ 9.22, 11; UD03 s = 4d, d = 3, perimeter 36; UD04 8π (10π, 16π, 32π); UD05 27 (54 checks); UD06 15 (trap 18, 2.31); UD07 PQ = 25, 7/25; UD08 r = 6 (3√2, 6√3 check); UD09 r = 3, 54 (18; 64 from r = h = 4); UD10 14 (10√2 ≈ 14.14); UD11 center (7, 4.5), r = 6.5; UD12 12 = 2·15·10/25; UD13 24 − 7 = 17.
math_errors.UB07 (rationale wording): The trap 6 is described as 'writes the vertex's x-coordinate as b/2, which flips the slope's sign'. The slope then comes out −b/2 = −3, so b = 6. Correct, but the explanation should show that step.
math_errors.UD08 (distractor C rationale): The arithmetic for C checks (legs r and r/√3 give area r²/(2√3) = 18√3, so r² = 108 and r = 6√3), but the stated misconception, 'AC = r and BC = r/√3', is implausible: it makes the hypotenuse 2r/√3, not 2r, so no student reasoning from a diameter of 2r gets there. Other natural slips collide with existing choices: taking AB = r gives r² = 144 and r = 12 (= D), and dropping the 1/2 gives 3√2 (= A). Fix: replace C with 36 (stops at r² = 36) or keep 6√3 with an honest rationale.

recommend_revise.UB03: Lower to easy-medium. The point plug-in (x = 3, y = 0) is a full bypass in this non-identity item. Keep it as a recognition item, or drop it if the batch already has a perimeter/plug-in-friendly item. Cite CLD-SAT-M-000089.
recommend_revise.UB05: Cite CLD-SAT-M-000794 (batch-073; exactly-one-solution parameter with a perfect-square discriminant) and keep UB05 in a different batch.
recommend_revise.UB14: Acknowledge the Desmos route (solve numerically, then evaluate 6^x = 24.000) and keep the item at medium (not medium-hard), or ask for the expression for 6^x in a form a calculator cannot read off.
recommend_revise.UB16: Optional: replace the weak D (6) with a factoring-slip value (e.g., −3 from (x + 2y)(x + 3y) sign errors, or 3/2).
recommend_revise.UD07: Keep ST = 50 only if the item reviewer accepts an intentionally unused given at easy level. Otherwise give the scale factor a role, e.g., ask for TU.
recommend_revise.UD08: Replace distractor C (6√3, implausible rationale) with 36 (stops at r² = 36) or another plausible slip that does not collide with A or D.
recommend_revise.UD12: Cite CLD-SAT-M-000855 (crossed wires, the same ab/(a + b) mechanism) and never batch the two together.
recommend_revise.UD13: Change the ladder and triple away from CLD-ACT-M-000241's 25-foot, 7-24-25 ladder (e.g., a 17-foot ladder with sin x° = 8/17 and cos y° = 8/17, answer 15 − 8 = 7), and cite 000801, 000802 and 000858 as the cofunction family.
